- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 18-day history + sentiment to smooth out short-term noise before forecasting.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model may misread momentum; apply “sentiment-weighted average” to forecast, giving more weight to recent sentiment peaks.
